changelog: The UI learns to speak. Translation layer Every player-visible string used to be an inline literal and the page was hard-coded English. There is now a translation layer under all of it: ~1,375 content strings — all 293 cards, medals, achievements, events, bosses and their dialogue, generals, elites, modifiers — plus 170 UI strings, a language picker that appears in Settings on its own the moment a second language exists, browser-language detection, and per-locale fonts. English pays nothing for it: the English lives at the call site, so an English build ships no dictionary at all. Turning it on found three bugs only a translation could have surfaced, all fixed. Card text wrapped on whitespace, so Chinese, Japanese and Thai card text became one unbreakable token and the fitter shrank it to nothing instead of wrapping. The bitmap glyph atlas is ASCII-only and emitted an empty string for anything outside it, so a translated general’s name would have rendered as nothing at all. And a power’s baked art was keyed off its English name, so renaming or translating it lost the art. Buttons are handed their labels 104 UI files had their English painted into the metal. All 103 that carry a word now have text-free art, and the game draws the label on top from the glyph atlas — so a button can say something different without new art being cut. Long labels stack onto two lines rather than shrinking into the plate, and each is measured to find the size that reads largest. It fixes something that was never about language, too: a button’s screen-reader name used to be its raw asset id, end_turn, and is now the actual word. New plate art Riveted medallions, and the tint carries meaning rather than decoration — green good, red bad, orange power, blue objective. The engraving and the wear are baked into the atlas rather than applied while drawing, so the lettering sits into the surface at no cost. The Engineer’s power is Surge It was Overcharge. Ten letters on a plate that also carries a full-height medallion and a value well left 197 pixels for the word; the type goes from 20px to 43px on the same plate, and the three power plates finally read as one set. Button, blurb and doctrine plaque now agree. Save data is untouched — this is a display name. Smaller download 20.4 MB of art no code path could reach any more — the replaced plate originals, and the source material the generator works from — no longer ships. Net effect of a release that added 331 files: about a megabyte. On the Mac The new labels are laid out in CSS container query units, which WebKit only learned in Safari 16. Every other platform is above that floor, but a Mac’s browser engine is whatever the OS carries — and the app had been declaring a minimum of macOS 10.13, which was never a decision, just a default nobody set. On an older Mac every label would have rendered as a slice through the middle of two enormous letters. The UI now detects the missing support and sets the label as plain text instead, and the app declares the macOS 11 minimum it has always claimed. Under the hood 918 tests. Notarized, stapled, Gatekeeper-clean, universal.
